newsitem.title: USA: U.S. insurers voice support for U.S.-Japan pact.
newsitem.headline: U.S. insurers voice support for U.S.-Japan pact.

text.p: U.S. insurers said they were encouraged by an announcement Tuesday that the United States and Japan have agreed to settle a dispute over the insurance market in Japan by the end of this year.
The interim pact, announced by Japanese officials late Monday night, allows U.S. insurers to begin direct marketing of automobile insurance immediately.

It also prevents subsidiaries of major Japanese life and non-life insurance companies from entering a profitable niche of the Japanese market before the end of the year while the two nations negotiate an overall agreement.
The niche, known as the third sector, covers areas such as personal accident, sickness and nursing care and has been a profitable market for foreign firms.
CIGNA Corp said it strongly supports the understanding announced today, saying it helps preserve the position of foreign companies in the third sector of the Japanese insurance market.

At the same time, the company said, the understanding represents an initial step toward substantial liberalization of Japan's two primary insurance sectors -- life and property & casualty -- by allowing direct sales of automobile insurance and increased flexibility for fire insurance.
American International Group Inc also said it was encouraged by the announcement, which seeks implementation of a U.S.-Japan Framework Agreement on insurance reached in 1994.
"The steps announced today, while modest and only first steps toward eventual full implementation of the agreement, are nonetheless important," AIG chairman Maurice Greenberg said.

"The Framework Agreement was intended to result in a more open insurance markeat in Japan, one that would benefit Japanese consumers, and at the same time would permit foreign insurers operating in Japan to increase their modest three percent share of the world's second largest insurance market," he said.
"The deregulation envisioned in the (1994) agreement remains to be achieved, but today's announcement is encouraging," he said.
Greenberg said he looks forward to further liberalization of direct auto, as well as in other product areas.
He said that would include the freedom to differentiate on the basis of rate, form and distribution, and would produce beneifts to Japanese consumers.

Both CIGNA and AIG operate insurance companies in Japan. Japan was AIG's largest overseas insurance market and its property-casualty operations were the leading foreign non-life insurer in Japan, according to the company's 1995 annual report.
CIGNA International operates both life and property and casualty companies in Japan.
